steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Performance Enhancing Drugs (PEDs): Substances used to improve sporting performance that are banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA). Taking PEDs is considered cheating because it gives an unfair advantage over clean competitors. | Stimulants: Drugs that increase alertness, reduce fatigue and increase aggression and competitiveness. They speed up the activity of the central nervous system. | Narcotic Analgesics: Painkilling drugs that mask the sensation of pain, allowing performers to continue training or competing despite injury. They work by blocking pain signals to the brain. | Anabolic Agents: Drugs that mimic the effects of the male hormone testosterone, promoting muscle growth (hypertrophy) and increasing strength. They also speed up recovery from intense training.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Name three types of performance enhancing drugs and explain the sporting advantage of each. | Explain how EPO and blood doping both improve endurance performance. What are the main health risks? | Why might a boxer use diuretics? Explain the advantage and the health risks.

steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Performance Enhancing Drugs (PEDs), Stimulants, Narcotic Analgesics, and one past-paper question.
